title: Concurrency is resolved before job-level if, so no-op runs can replace pending runs in a shared group
answers: a notification never appears after a second label was added
a review request was dropped by a later event
why does a skipped run cancel a useful run
workflow concurrency applied before the job condition
body:
Symptom: A PR does not get its expected bot action, such as the autoformat guidance comment or the Copilot review request, because a later unrelated event ran first.
Root cause: Workflow-level `concurrency` is resolved before the job-level `if`. A run whose job will skip still occupies the group slot, and a pending run in the same group is replaced by it. cancel-in-progress: false protects only the running run.
Fix pattern: Choose the group key so that events sharing it take the same code path. Do not add a compound key such as label name or event action to a shared group; the PR review chose to switch those workflows to `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` instead.
Constraints: This matters only when the job `if` filters events the group does not, such as label names or review_requested on non-draft PRs. Workflows that use the PR-number group must have no such filtered jobs.
applies: Choosing or editing a concurrency group in a workflow whose job-level `if` filters on event details such as action, label name or draft state.
says: The pull request did not receive the automated code formatting comment after applying a label.
Automated Copilot review request never triggered when the pull request was marked ready.
Adding a second label caused the bot notification comment to be skipped completely.
Ensure automated pull request bot feedback is posted even when other events occur simultaneously.
Reviewer bot request dropped when an unrelated change was made to the pull request.
search: Workflow concurrency resolution occurs before job-level if conditions, allowing a pending run in a shared group to be replaced by a run whose job skips. To prevent no-op runs from cancelling pending bot actions like autoformat comments or Copilot review requests, workflows switch to group: ${{ github.run_id }} instead of compound keys containing label names or event actions. This constraint applies when job-level if conditions filter events like label names or review_requested on non-draft PRs, whereas PR-number groups require jobs with no such event filtering. Setting cancel-in-progress: false protects only the active running job, applying to .github/workflows/autoformat-label-notify.yml and .github/workflows/copilot-review.yml.
